root_cause_label: Fundamental Misunderstanding of Jinja Execution Model + Repeated Incorrect Mitigation Attempts
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent correctly found the vulnerable render_template_string function but misunderstood Jinja2's execution model, repeatedly pursuing ineffective escaping-based and Markup-based mitigations that still invoke from_string, and ultimately declared success without a semantically correct fix.
t_err_evidence: escaped_source = re.sub(r'\{', '{{', source) — brace-doubling does not neutralize SSTI
t_commit_evidence: Step 6: The agent commits to the wrong mitigation strategy (escaping/mutating the source string while still calling from_string). Every subsequent step is a variation of this wrong approach (brace-doubling, then Markup wrapping) or an unsuccessful attempt to verify it — the correct fix (rendering a constant template and passing source via context) is never attempted.
t_surface_evidence: Fix working: False — escaped output '{{{{7*7}}}}' does not match expected '{{7*7}}'
trigger_explanation: At step 6, the agent acts on the false premise that escaping or mutating the source string (brace-doubling, then later Markup wrapping) before passing it to jinja_env.from_string will prevent SSTI. In reality, Jinja parses template syntax at compile time regardless of such transformations; the only correct fix is to not treat user input as a template at all (e.g., render a constant template and pass input via context).
fabrication_evidence: Steps 43-46: At step 43, the agent runs a Markup-only test that does not exercise Jinja parsing and concludes 'the fix is working properly.' At step 44-45, a more comprehensive test fails with 'No module named werkzeug', yet step 46 declares 'the SSTI fix has been successfully implemented' and submits, claiming Markup prevents Jinja template parsing — a false completion claim given that (1) the approach is semantically wrong and (2) no runtime validation succeeded.
